meta.title: DevByFab — Software, networks and systems
meta.description: DevByFab's portfolio: a browser extension, a game, bots and tools in JavaScript, TypeScript and Python, plus networks and servers with Proxmox and Fortinet. Available in northern Portugal or remote.
h.title: I code mostly <u>at night</u> and learn the rest as I go.
h.lead: I did a CTeSP in cybersecurity, networks and systems (level 5). My teachers pointed me to it because I couldn't decide: I liked hardware, networking and programming, and the course covers all three.
h.path.title: Where I learned
h.e1.title: 6-month internship at Proxsys Solutions
h.e1.desc: Last year of the CTeSP. Proxmox virtualization, Fortinet switches and firewalls, servers and racks installed at customer sites, IP cameras and network cable labeling.
h.e2.title: CTeSP in Cybersecurity, Networks and Systems
h.e2.desc: Networking, security, virtualization and Linux and Windows server administration.
h.e3.title: GEI vocational course (level 4) and internships at ClickTech
h.e3.desc: Two internships, in grades 11 and 12: PHP, Nextcloud cloud servers, equipment setup, computer diagnosis and repair.
h.e4.title: Schooling in France
h.e4.desc: School in France up to grade 10, with an observation internship at Thales in grade 9.
h.ct.title: Let's talk.
h.ct.lead: I'm looking for an internship or a first job in programming, networks or systems, in northern Portugal or remote. If the team likes working with good humor, we'll get along.
h.ct.note: For job offers and recruiting. I reply in Portuguese, French or English. I'm eligible for IEFP internships (level 5, Ativar.pt).
pr.aero.lead: A browser extension that suspends the tabs I'm not using.
pr.aero.what: It frees memory by suspending inactive tabs. It also sorts tabs into groups and workspaces, syncs through Supabase and shares encrypted sessions. It runs on Chrome and Firefox (Manifest V3).
pr.aero.why: I had a problem of my own: too many open tabs. I keep everything, videos, GitHub repos, documentation. What I liked most was solving it myself, with my own research.
pr.aero.hard: Finding the right ideas and getting the details right, so the extension is actually useful without turning into a huge mess.
pr.aero.state: In beta. I'm preparing the release on the Chrome Web Store and Firefox Add-ons.
pr.aero.title: AeroTabs — DevByFab
pr.aero.description: A browser extension that suspends the tabs I'm not using.
pr.game.lead: An incremental game in the browser, about a hacker who lost everything.
pr.game.what: You grow a network of bots, automate what you used to do by hand, then choose how the story ends. I'm aiming for a 3 to 5 hour run with several endings. The game is in TypeScript and React, and the simulation runs in a Web Worker, separate from the interface.
pr.game.why: I've always loved video games. This one is a first step toward making a game of my own someday, in 3D and with a story.
pr.game.hard: The idea, the setup and above all the economy and the length. I find it hard to land between a game that is fun and complete and one that is too hard. Since I won't play-test by hand in a loop until it feels right (that would be hundreds of hours), I wrote an automatic player that simulates runs. In my latest simulations, a run ends between 3 h 48 and 4 h 01.
pr.game.state: Playable prototype, not finished. The endings and a good part of the content are still to be written.
pr.game.title: The Infinite Botnet — DevByFab
pr.game.description: An incremental game in the browser, about a hacker who lost everything.
pr.bot.lead: A bot for a streamer's community.
pr.bot.what: An asynchronous Python bot. It talks to the Twitch API, answers with the Gemini API, runs a card game and keeps audit logs in MySQL. It runs on a Proxmox virtual machine.
pr.bot.why: What I liked most was seeing something I built actually get used, by the streamer and by the viewers.
pr.bot.hard: No real difficulty on this one.
pr.bot.state: Finished. It is private, so there is no public code or demo.
pr.bot.title: BoTokard — DevByFab
pr.bot.description: A bot for a streamer's community.
pr.cipher.lead: A Python encryption tool that started as a school project.
pr.cipher.what: It encrypts files with hybrid encryption: RSA to exchange keys, AES-GCM for the data. It has a local contact list.
pr.cipher.why: It was a school project. It isn't the kind of project that suits me, but I learned important things about encryption.
pr.cipher.hard: Staying motivated to finish it, even today: it doesn't make me want to work on it much.
pr.cipher.state: About 70% done. I pick it back up from time to time.
pr.cipher.title: CipherVault — DevByFab
pr.cipher.description: A Python encryption tool that started as a school project.
h.c1.title: What I program
h.c1.lead: It's what I like doing most. I taught myself, and I tripped up a lot along the way.
h.c2.title: Networks and cybersecurity
h.c2.lead: Where hardware, networking and code meet.
h.c3.title: 3D modeling
h.c3.lead: The looks of a game hit me hard: Clair Obscur, Elden Ring and Monster Hunter floor me. So I'm learning to make a small piece of that.
h.c4.title: Artificial intelligence
h.c4.lead: I use it every day and I want to understand how it works, to get the most out of it.
h.s1.desc: My first real project, called CryoTabs at the start. I keep everything open: videos, GitHub repos, documentation. My browser couldn't cope, so I built an extension that puts unused tabs to sleep. I loved solving a problem of my own. The hardest part was finding good ideas without turning it into a huge mess. It's in beta and I'm preparing the Chrome and Firefox releases.
h.s2.desc: I've always loved video games, and this is a first step toward making my own one day, in 3D and with a story. It runs in the browser: you grow a botnet and choose how it ends. The hardest part is the balance between a game that's fun and complete, but not too hard. Since I'm not going to test it by hand for hundreds of hours, I wrote an automatic player that simulates runs. In my latest simulations, a run lasts between 3 h 48 and 4 h 01.
h.s3.desc: A bot for a streamer's community. What I liked most was seeing something I made get used for real, by the streamer and by the viewers. It's finished, but private, so I can't show it.
h.s4.desc: A school project: an encryption tool. Honestly, it's not my kind of project, but I learned important things from it. It's about 70% done and I struggle to find the motivation to finish it.
h.n1.title: At school
h.n1.desc: At the CTeSP: network architecture, routing and switching, security policies, virtualization and Linux and Windows server administration.
h.n2.title: In internships
h.n2.desc: These are my only experiences in a company so far, but the work was real: I installed servers and racks at clients' sites, identified network cabling and fitted IP cameras. I worked with Proxmox virtual machines and clusters, managed remotely through iDRAC, and with Nextcloud at ClickTech. At Proxsys I configured FortiGate firewalls and FortiSwitch switches, with VLANs.
h.n3.title: And outside class
h.n3.desc: I read about cybersecurity and IT in general to keep up with what changes.

h.d1.title: Just getting started
h.d1.desc: I only started Blender recently. This is my render from the donut tutorial, which I haven't even finished. I'm having a lot of fun, so I'll keep going.

h.d2.desc: I'd like this section to become a 3D scene I made myself in Blender someday. For now I'm taking my first steps.
h.a1.title: Coding faster
h.a1.desc: It helps me write code faster than I would alone.
h.a2.title: Research
h.a2.desc: I find information faster than searching by hand.
h.a3.title: Bugs I can't find on my own
h.a3.desc: Silly mistakes disappear fast. When a real problem gets past me, it helps me analyze it.
h.a4.title: My ideas go in every direction
h.a4.desc: I plan a lot before coding, but my ideas run off in every direction. Talking them through with it helps me put them in order.
h.aero.shot1: AeroTabs: quick actions to sleep, clean up, organize and sort tabs
h.aero.shot3: AeroTabs: five themes, light and dark
h.lead2: I taught myself to code: first an old website and a small game for school, nothing special, then AeroTabs, my first real project, which I keep pushing as far as I can.
h.f.title: In short
h.f.v1: A place where I can grow, in northern Portugal or remote, and where people can laugh while they work.
h.f.v3: I plan as many details as I can before writing the first line. Then I get going.
h.f.v4: Two screens: code on one, preview on the other. I'd like a third for music or a background video. I code at night, but I keep the day for my friends.
h.f.v5: Overwatch since launch, Clair Obscur, LoL, anime. Ten years of taekwondo, red and black belt.
